Sam: hey folks :wave: I'm opening my very first PR and CI keeps failing on lint/tests. Where's the canonical CONTRIBUTING/style guide and what naming/merge rules should I follow?

Taylor: welcome aboard! :tada: The short version: CONTRIBUTING.md at https://redwood.internal/dev/contributing has the guide. Branches: feat/<JIRA-123>-short-desc, fix/<JIRA-123>-short-desc, chore/<ticket>. Use kebab-case. PR title should start with the ticket in brackets e.g. [ENG-234] Short summary. Squash merges only.

Ben: common fixes: run the linter & formatter locally: 
```
npm ci
npm run lint -- --fix
npm run format
```
We also have pre-commit hooks (husky) and a .pre-commit-config.yaml. If you have staged files that fail, the hook will stop the commit.

Maya: small additions: we follow conventional commits for CHANGELOG automation (feat:, fix:, chore:). If the change is user-facing add a one-line changelog entry under the PR body with the tag `CHANGELOG:`. If internal, put `CHANGELOG: skip`.

ci-bot: Build #4587 · redwood/redwood-ci · failed · eslint error in packages/ui/src/Button.tsx:12 · https://ci.redwood/build/4587

Sam: ok I fixed the linting and pushed a new commit. Quick Q: how many reviewers do I need and any expectations for review scope?

Taylor: default: 2 reviewers for core services, 1 reviewer OK for most frontend & infra changes. At least one review from a CODEOWNER path for affected files. Keep PRs focused: 'what' + 'why' + testing steps in the body.

Ben: try to keep PRs <400 lines if possible. For large refactors, break into smaller follow-ups (API contract change first, then implementation). Add unit tests where relevant and mark flaky tests in the PR description if you had to touch them.

Sam: branch protection — do we need a special label like `merge-on-green`?

Taylor: we run an auto-merge bot. Either add the `merge-on-green` label or request it in a comment with @ci-bot and the bot will queue merge after CI passes and required approvals present. Also resolve conflicts before merge.

Maya: formatting tips: run `npm run format` or `pnpm -w format` depending on the repo. If prettier changes lots of files, split the PR: one for formatting (mention in title) and another for the real change.

Sam: thanks everyone, that helps a lot. One last thing — any recommended local smoke commands to run quickly?

Ben: yes, quick smoke: `./scripts/smoke.sh` (runs lint + unit quick filter) or `npm run test:watch` for iterating. If CI fails with a flaky test, try `./tools/repro-flake.sh <test-name>` and open a ticket if it reproduces.

Taylor: ping me or drop in #devex if you want a 15m pairing session for the PR. Also check docs in the repo root (CONTRIBUTING.md) and our internal runbook for CI troubleshooting. :thumbsup:

Sam: will do — appreciate it! :raised_hands:
